marks.gloss_en: מדאמר רחמנא נבלה לא תאכל -- if a dying animal were forbidden while alive, need it be said after death?
the verse: you shall not eat a carcass (Deut 14:21)
ודלמא היינו נבלה היינו מסוכנת? -- perhaps 'carcass' is itself the dying animal
ודלמא לעולם: carcass and dying animal are one status -- alive it is forbidden by a positive command, after death by a prohibition (unanswered; the text turns with אלא)
מדאמר רחמנא טרפה לא תאכל -- if the dying animal, which lacks nothing, were forbidden, need the tereifa be?
the verse: you shall not eat a tereifa (Ex 22:30)
ודלמא היינו טרפה היינו מסוכנת, to violate a positive command and a prohibition
ודלמא carcass = tereifa = dying animal, to violate two prohibitions and a positive command (unanswered; the text turns with אלא)
RSBG: [a dying animal's slaughter is valid only] once it convulses with hand and foot
the mishna: a small animal that extended its foreleg and did not draw it back -- invalid, for that is only the soul's departure
[a slaughtered] animal in danger of dying is permitted -- the presupposition the Gemara seeks a source for
'the fat of a carcass and the fat of a tereifa' (Lev 7:24) -- and the Master said: let the carcass prohibition, and the tereifa prohibition, take effect upon the prohibition of forbidden fat
